_comment: Static snapshot based on CGWB-published block classifications (Central Ground Water Board / India-WRIS 2023-2024). Not a live feed — see TRD section 2.3 for rationale.

v-ballarpur.notes: Intense industrial draw and thermal cooling demands have lowered shallow unconfined aquifer levels by 1.8m over 5 years.

v-chandrapur-east.notes: Paved surface run-off prevents local recharge; deep tube-wells running dry during May peak.

v-warora.notes: Extensive cotton irrigation creates severe pre-monsoon drawdown.

v-bhadravati.notes: Mine dewatering cones of depression impact surrounding village handpumps.

v-mul.notes: Canal command area and river recharge maintain healthy groundwater buffers.

v-rajura.notes: Hard limestone strata limits infiltration; fracture zones experience rapid drying.

v-chimur.notes: Forest catchment preserves water retention in natural swales.

v-brahmapuri.notes: High water table near Wainganga basin; susceptible to waterlogging during heavy rain.

v-sindewahi.notes: Rice-paddy irrigation tanks support post-monsoon aquifer stability.

v-korpana.notes: Elevated fluoride concentrations and diminishing water table in basalt zones.

v-pombhurna.notes: Balanced extraction; village tanks maintain adequate percolation.

v-nagbhid.notes: Multiple historic tanks (Malguzari tanks) provide resilient surface-groundwater coupling.

v-bm-balotra.notes: Deep sand aquifers depleted by industrial textile dyeing and domestic reliance.

v-bm-chohtan.notes: Severe dune aquifer exhaustion; static water levels drop beyond 45 meters.

v-bm-sheo.notes: Deep saline pockets limit accessible fresh water; beris (traditional step structures) stressed.

v-bm-baytu.notes: Open-pit extraction cones of depression lower surrounding village wells.

v-bm-siwana.notes: Granite basement rock offers narrow fracture storage; rapid post-monsoon depletion.

v-bm-gudamalani.notes: Luni riverbed alluvium sustains only shallow seasonal pumping before drying.

v-bm-sindhari.notes: High total dissolved solids (TDS) and salinity render deeper borewells non-potable.

v-wy-meppadi.notes: High precipitation recharges laterite slopes rapidly; risk is oversaturation rather than depletion.

v-wy-vythiri.notes: Western Ghats rain belt ensures high water table; perched water tables during monsoon.

v-wy-mananthavady.notes: Kabini river basin maintains steady sub-surface recharge year round.

v-wy-panamaram.notes: Valley floor aquifer saturated; susceptible to surface waterlogging.

v-wy-sulthan-bathery.notes: Plateau terrain with stable dug well levels and moderate seasonal variation.

v-wy-kalpetta.notes: Granite gneiss rock mass holds localized fracture water adequate for municipal supply.

v-sb-gosaba.notes: Shallow aquifer is hyper-saline; fresh water confined to deep 250m+ sand layers, severely vulnerable to storm surge salinization.

v-sb-basanti.notes: High groundwater table but non-potable due to tidal salinity ingress; fresh lenses under threat.

v-sb-canning.notes: Heavy extraction by fish-processing units causing local cone of salinity depression.

v-sb-kakdwip.notes: Coastal sand ridges hold thin freshwater lenses prone to cyclone sea-water overflow.

v-sb-sagar.notes: Island perimeter erosion allows seawater penetration into unconfined domestic tanks.

v-so-pandharpur.notes: Intensive sugarcane cultivation along Bhima basin over-drafts deep basalt aquifers.

v-so-sangole.notes: Pomegranate orchard distress; deepest borewells in Solapur suffering complete summer failure.

v-so-karmala.notes: Rainshadow drought tract with high summer evaporation and failing dug wells.

v-so-barshi.notes: Pulse processing mills and dense population deplete urban boundary borewells.

v-so-mangalwedha.notes: Chronic agrarian water deficit; village water tankers active from March to June.
